steps.ask: Why would a straight-line measure give a value close to 0 for a curved pattern?
steps.title: Explain why r can be close to 0 in part (b)

lines.text: The correlation coefficient measures how well the points fit a straight line. These points follow a quadratic (U-shaped) curve, which is symmetrical, so no straight line fits them and $r_{FS}$ is close to 0.

lesson.final: r = \hl{3}{0.966};\ \text{correlation measures linear relationships, and this data is quadratic}

steps.title: (i) List the red cubes and find their total

lines.text: Red cubes per trial (A to G): $0, 3, 2, 2, 4, 5, 1$.

steps.title: (i) Find the sum of the squares of the red values

lines.text: Use $\sigma^2 = \dfrac{\sum x^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2$.
Let $x$ be the red cubes and $y$ the green cubes, with $n = 7$. Green cubes per trial: $4, 2, 0, 3, 0, 0, 2$.

lines.tex: r &= \frac{n\sum xy - \sum x \sum y}{\sqrt{\left(n\sum x^2 - (\sum x)^2\right)\left(n\sum y^2 - (\sum y)^2\right)}}

steps.title: (iii) Explain why the correlation is negative

lines.text: Each trial picks exactly $5$ cubes, so the red, green and blue counts always add to $5$.
If a trial has more red cubes, there is less room for green cubes, so fewer green cubes are likely.
As the number of red cubes increases, the number of green cubes tends to decrease, so the correlation coefficient is negative.

steps.ask: D and E add to 25. Which pairs fit the ordering rules?
steps.title: Split D + E and B + C

lines.text: $D + E = 25$ with $D < E$ and a gap of at least 2: $D = 12, E = 13$ fails (gap 1) and $D = 10, E = 15$ fails because $F = 16$ is only 1 above 15. So $D = 11$, $E = 14$.

$B + C = 15$ with $C \le 9$ (a gap of at least 2 below $D = 11$) and $B \ge 6$ (a gap of at least 2 above $A = 4$): $B = 6$, $C = 9$. (B = 7, C = 8 is not allowed because $C$ must be at least 2 more than $B$, so $C \ge B + 2$. With $B + C = 15$ this gives $B \le 6.5$, and with $B \ge 6$ this forces $B = 6$.)
